City council votes to keep the night buses

By A. Reporter, transport correspondent19 May 2026
Share this articleShare on TwitterShare on FacebookEmail a friend

The city council voted on Tuesday evening to keep all eleven night bus routes running, reversing a proposal that would have cut seven of them from September. The vote was 34 to 21, with four abstentions.

The proposal had been on the table since the transport budget was published in February, and had drawn objections from hospital staff, hospitality workers and the two universities, all of whom argued that the routes carry people who have no alternative at four in the morning.

Councillor M. Adeyemi, who moved the amendment, said the original figures had measured the wrong thing. The routes were assessed on fares collected per journey, which she said counts a nurse going to a night shift the same way it counts an empty seat at noon.

What changes in September

Nothing, for passengers. All eleven routes keep their current frequency until at least the next budget, and the two routes that were due to be shortened will run their full length.

The council will fund the gap from the parking surplus rather than the general transport budget, a mechanism the finance committee described as workable for one year and not for three.

What happens next

A review of how routes are assessed is due before the next budget. The council has committed to publishing the methodology it uses, which the opposition had asked for twice.

The transport authority said it would begin recruiting the twelve drivers it had stopped hiring in March.
